name: Acacia acinacea
description: A small to medium shrub with small elliptic phyllodes and golden globular flower heads in spring. It needs good drainage in gardens.
pruning: Pruning after flowering is beneficial.

name: Acacia baileyana
description: A fast-growing small tree with silvery, fern-like leaves and masses of golden flowers in late winter. It is a weed outside its tiny natural range.
pruning: It keeps its shape best when pruned hard after flowering.
care_note: It is an environmental weed (declared in the ACT); please do not plant it near bushland, and seedlings can be pulled by hand.

name: Acacia complanata
description: A large, somewhat open shrub with flattened, winged stems, sometimes 5 to 6 m tall. It regrows from a lignotuber after fire.
pruning: It can be pruned to the size wanted, and light pruning from the start gives a shapelier shrub.

name: Acacia dealbata
description: A tall wattle with silvery blue-grey feathery leaves and bright yellow flower balls in late winter and spring.

name: Acacia decurrens
description: A fast-growing wattle with feathery leaves and green winged branchlets that is covered in yellow flower balls. It is short-lived and may be too big for some gardens.
care_note: It tends to be short-lived, is prone to borer attack, and can naturalise outside its natural area.

name: Acacia genistifolia
description: A small to medium prickly shrub with narrow stiff phyllodes and cream to pale yellow flower heads. It makes an informal hedge and shelters small birds.
care_note: Its sharp phyllodes can deter access to an area.

name: Acacia implexa
description: A small to medium tree, often spreading or weeping, with cream flowers mostly in summer after other wattles have finished. It is very hardy and long-lived.
pruning: Occasional pruning is likely to improve flowering in following years.

name: Acacia leiocalyx
description: A shrub or small tree with sickle-shaped phyllodes and pale yellow cylindrical flower heads from winter into spring. It grows in eucalypt woodland on well-drained shallow soils and is short-lived.

name: Acacia longifolia
description: A tall shrub or small tree with long, bright green phyllodes and golden flower spikes from late winter to spring. It is useful for erosion control and windbreaks but has become a serious weed in some areas.
pruning: A light prune after flowering keeps it bushy.
care_note: It is a serious weed in Western Australia and an environmental weed elsewhere, so avoid planting near bushland.

name: Acacia maidenii
description: A tree 5 to 20 m tall growing on the margins of rainforest and wet forest.

name: Acacia mearnsii
description: A tree to 10 m or more with fine dark green feathery leaves and fragrant pale yellow flower heads in late spring. It is easy to grow but spreads beyond its natural range.
care_note: It is a serious weed in some places and is naturalised in WA, so avoid planting it near bushland.

name: Acacia melanoxylon
description: A large, long-lived evergreen tree with dark green phyllodes and cream to yellow ball flowers in winter and spring. It suits large blocks and reserves, but not close to pipes or power lines.
care_note: Keep it at least 3.5 m from sewer pipes; it is a pest in some Tasmanian regions.

name: Acacia mucronata
description: A wattle found in the south coast and southern tablelands of New South Wales, in Victoria and in Tasmania. The subspecies in New South Wales is subspecies longifolia.

name: Acacia paradoxa
description: A prickly, spreading wattle with small phyllodes and yellow ball flowers. It makes a tough hedge or screen and copes with salt spray.
care_note: Its stipules are thorn-like, so keep it away from paths.

name: Acacia salicina
description: A shrub or tree 3 to 10 m high (sometimes 20 m) found along creek banks in dry inland forest and woodland.

name: Acacia saligna
description: A fast-growing wattle with drooping, willow-like branches and yellow flowers in late winter. It is native to Western Australia but is a weed in many places in the eastern states.
care_note: It self-sows and suckers freely and spreads into bushland, so avoid using it near bushland in the eastern states.

name: Acacia stricta
description: An erect or spreading shrub or tree, 1 to 6 m, of forest, woodland and heath, mostly in the ranges.

name: Acacia suaveolens
description: A sparse, straggly shrub with blue-grey phyllodes and sweetly scented cream flowers in autumn to spring. It prefers sandy soil.
pruning: Pruning promotes more flowering branches.
care_note: It is reported to be toxic to stock.

name: Acacia tetragonophylla
description: A tough, prickly, single-trunked arid shrub with yellow flowers in winter and spring. It tolerates drought and heavy frost.
care_note: Its prickles are sharp, so please keep it away from paths.

name: Acacia ulicifolia
description: A rounded, prickly shrub with needle-like phyllodes and cream flower balls in winter and spring. It suits low-maintenance sites and hedges.
care_note: Its sharp phyllodes make it a prickly plant.

name: Acacia verticillata
description: A rounded shrub with dark green, spine-like phyllodes in whorls and pale yellow flower spikes. It is hardy and works as a hedge or screen.
pruning: It can be pruned for a more compact form.

name: Acaena novae-zelandiae
description: A creeping herb with globular burr-like flower heads that stick to clothing.

name: Acrotriche serrulata
description: A dwarf, spreading, prickly-leaved shrub with fragrant green flowers whose nectar pots give it its name. It suits rockeries and mixed beds.
edible: The flowers and fruits were eaten by Aboriginal people for their nectar.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil.

name: Adiantum aethiopicum
description: A fine rhizomatous fern forming colonies in moist, sheltered places. It is popular in cultivation and can become weedy by spores.
pruning: It dies down in winter, so cut it back hard to encourage new spring growth.

name: Adiantum formosum
description: A large maidenhair fern with fronds 60 to 120 cm long that spreads by a long creeping rhizome into colonies. It suits moist, shaded spots under trees or along streams.

name: Adiantum hispidulum
description: A small, upright fern with rough, hairy stalks and fan-shaped leaflets, pink when young. It is hardy and does well in pots.
care_note: It likes plenty of moisture but should not be kept over-wet; it tolerates drying out better than most ferns.

name: Alphitonia excelsa
description: A fast-growing tree with glossy dark green leaves that are silvery underneath. It is used for screening and bush regeneration.

name: Alyxia ruscifolia
description: A stiff, rounded shrub with whorled, sharp-pointed dark leaves, scented white flowers and orange berries in chains. It is hardy and suits shady spots.
care_note: The fruit is thought to be poisonous, and the plant bleeds milky sap if damaged.

name: Amyema cambagei
description: A native mistletoe that grows on she-oaks (Casuarinaceae) in forest and woodland, forming spreading to hanging clumps. It cannot be grown on its own.

name: Amyema congener
description: A native mistletoe that grows on other trees, commonly Acacia and Casuarinaceae, with leathery leaves. It is not a plant to grow in the ground.
care_note: It is a parasite on host trees.

name: Amyema pendula
description: A hanging mistletoe that grows on the branches of many eucalypts and some wattles, with long narrow leaves and tubular flowers. It is a native parasite and not a plant to grow in a bed.

name: Angophora hispida
description: A small tree or large shrub with large clusters of white flowers in summer, common on sandstone soils around Sydney.
care_note: It flowers best in full sun and is hardy in a variety of well-drained soils.

name: Anigozanthos humilis
description: A short kangaroo paw with leaves rarely over 300 mm and mainly yellow, sometimes orange or red, spring flowers. It can be grown even where humid summers defeat other western plants, though it is short-lived there.
care_note: It needs a well-drained position and may die back to its rhizome after flowering; a low-phosphorus fertiliser after flowering helps.

name: Aotus ericoides
description: An upright shrub with small variable leaves with rolled margins and yellow-orange pea flowers in spring.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil.

name: Aphananthe philippinensis
description: A rainforest tree with stiff, toothed, rough leaves and yellow fruit that ripens in autumn, found along streams and on alluvial flats.

name: Araucaria bidwillii
description: A very tall conifer with a dome-shaped crown and football-sized cones holding edible nuts. It tolerates cold and should not be planted where falling cones can hit people.
edible: The nuts from the female cones can be eaten raw or roasted, or ground into flour.
care_note: Falling cones can injure people, so keep an exclusion zone around a tree bearing cones.

name: Araucaria cunninghamii
description: A tall, slow-growing conifer with a cone-shaped crown and bark in horizontal hoops. It needs a lot of room and regular watering in its first two years.
care_note: It needs regular watering for the first two years in the ground and plenty of space.

name: Arthropodium strictum
description: A small clumping lily with mauve, star-shaped flowers that smell of chocolate on warm days. It is good in mass plantings and tolerates drought.
edible: Indigenous peoples used the tubers for food.

name: Asplenium australasicum
description: A large fern whose spreading fronds form a deep saucer-shaped crown, growing on trees, rocks or in organic soil. It suits containers, indoors or out.
care_note: It needs plenty of moisture but good drainage, because it rots in poorly drained soil.

name: Atriplex cinerea
description: An erect or spreading shrub with silvery grey-green leaves that grows on coastal sands. It suits exposed salty coastal sites.

name: Avicennia marina
description: A small tree or shrub of salty estuaries with greyish leaf undersides. It is the commonest mangrove in NSW.

name: Backhousia myrtifolia
description: A lilly-pilly-like tree with dark green leaves that smell of cinnamon when crushed and clusters of creamy-white flowers. It makes dense shade and is long-lived, though it needs room to spread.
care_note: It may be susceptible to myrtle rust.

name: Banksia dallanneyi
description: A prostrate to low shrub that spreads by underground stems, with long deeply lobed leaves and orange-brown flower heads. It is one of the more reliable species in areas without humid, wet summers.
care_note: It does best where summers are not humid and wet.

name: Banksia grandis
description: A small tree or large shrub from south-west Western Australia with very large, deeply lobed leaves and tall, pale yellow flower spikes in spring and summer. It attracts nectar-feeding birds, bees and insects but is slow to flower from seed.
care_note: It is sensitive to phosphorus and dislikes humid summers, so use a native fertiliser and well-drained sandy soil.

name: Banksia oblongifolia
description: A small, fairly open shrub with fern-like leaves and yellow flower spikes in autumn and winter. Its modest size suits small gardens and containers, and birds visit the flowers.
care_note: It is sensitive to phosphorus, so use a native plant fertiliser and well-drained soil.

name: Banksia ornata
description: A spreading, bushy banksia with yellow cylindrical flower spikes that age to bronze. It suits sandy, well-drained gardens and draws nectar-feeding birds.
care_note: It is very intolerant of heavy soils, so plant it in well-drained sand or loam, in raised beds if needed.

name: Bauera rubioides
description: A bushy shrub with pink or white flowers mainly in spring, growing along creeklines. It is short-lived unless it gets moist, well-drained conditions.
pruning: Prune after flowering to keep it compact.

name: Bedfordia arborescens
description: A shrub or small tree of wet forest and rainforest margins, with leaves densely white and woolly underneath. Orange flower heads appear in spring.

name: Billardiera mutabilis
description: A slender twining shrub with silky new shoots and green-yellow flowers that turn navy blue with age, followed by green berries. It grows in moist coastal eucalypt forest.

name: Blechnum nudum
description: A tufted ground fern with erect, pinnate fronds that can form a short fibrous trunk with age. It grows beside creeks and water features and in moist shady gardens.
care_note: It likes moist, well-composted soil and may need extra water in dry spells.

name: Bossiaea prostrata
description: A low, evergreen, spreading groundcover with orange pea flowers in spring. It is used for weed suppression, rockeries and embankments.

name: Breynia oblongifolia
description: A hardy shrub with small green flowers and berries that ripen from orange to black, eaten by birds. It tolerates a range of soils.

toxic.note: The berries are toxic if eaten and can irritate pets.

name: Burchardia umbellata
description: A grass-like perennial that dies back in winter and sends up umbels of white to pale pink flowers with reddish centres in spring. It suits cottage gardens, gaps between shrubs and containers, though nurseries rarely sell it.
edible: First Nations people ate the tubers, raw or cooked.

name: Callicoma serratifolia
description: A bushy shrub or small tree with serrated leaves and round, lime-yellow wattle-like flower balls in late spring. It likes moist ground, such as the shelter of a house's south side.
care_note: Young plants are frost tender and it needs plenty of moisture.

name: Callitris gracilis
description: A conical tree to 20 m with tiny scale leaves and persistent woody cones. It grows in open woodland on sandy rises.

name: Callitris rhomboidea
description: A small conifer that grows into a pyramid shape when mature. Its dense foliage gives small native birds nesting sites.
pruning: It responds poorly to pruning and can hold dead wood, so shape it only while young.
care_note: It is drought tolerant once established, which makes it more vulnerable in prolonged droughts.

name: Canavalia rosea
description: A climbing or trailing herb with stems 2 to 3 m long that grows on coastal sand dunes and flowers most of the year.

name: Capparis arborea
description: A shrub to small tree with fragrant white flowers with long stamens and edible caper-like fruit. It is hardy once established and feeds caper white butterfly caterpillars.
care_note: Young plants scramble using sharp thorns.

name: Cassinia aculeata
description: An erect shrub with narrow leaves and large flat clusters of small cream flower heads in summer. It often colonises ground after fire or logging.

name: Cassinia longifolia
description: A strongly scented, sticky shrub with large clusters of creamy flower heads from summer to autumn, found on ridges in forest and disturbed ground.

name: Cassinia sifton
description: A multi-stemmed shrub with narrow leaves and large, drooping plumes of deep red to brown flower heads. It is a pioneer plant of disturbed ground.

name: Castanospermum australe
description: A large rainforest tree with red and yellow pea flowers in spring and big pods in autumn, grown as a shade tree in parks and large gardens.
care_note: The seeds are poisonous and cause vomiting and diarrhoea unless extensively processed.

name: Casuarina glauca
description: A tree with drooping grey-green branchlets that often sends up root suckers and forms pure stands. It grows in brackish places along estuaries and streams near the coast.

name: Ceratopetalum apetalum
description: A medium-sized rainforest tree of cool and warm temperate forest on the east coast. It flowers in spring and summer.

name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
description: A large shrub to small tree that flowers in November and December, after which the sepals turn red and are shed in February. It grows best in well-drained sandy soil.
pruning: Prune after flowering to control shape and height and make a denser plant.

name: Chenopodium parabolicum
description: A dense, spreading evergreen shrub with mealy foliage and small green flowers. It is a hardy, low-maintenance screen that gives small birds and lizards shelter.
pruning: Prune to promote bushy foliage.
care_note: It needs very good drainage.

name: Chloris truncata
description: A native perennial grass to about 50 cm that forms a dense low crown and flowers in response to rain. It grows on many soils and is more common on red or black earths.

name: Chrysocephalum baxteri
description: A low, silvery perennial with white-bracted flower heads with yellow centres over a long season. It suits sunny, well-drained spots.
pruning: Cut it back after flowering if it becomes untidy.

name: Chrysocephalum semipapposum
description: A variable, aromatic perennial herb with grey stems and clusters of small, bright yellow button flowers from spring. It dies back in dry spells and shoots again after rain.

name: Clematis aristata
description: A leaf climber with trifoliate leaves and starry white to cream flowers, followed by fluffy seed heads on female plants. It is vigorous but unlikely to smother other plants.
pruning: It withstands heavy pruning.

name: Clematis microphylla
description: A fine-leaved vine with creamy-white flowers followed by fluffy seed heads. It is hardy in heat, dry spells and heavy frost.

name: Clerodendrum floribundum
description: A shrub or tree 2 to 10 m tall found on the margins of coastal rainforest in northern NSW and further north.

name: Coleus australis
description: A low, prostrate to semi-erect sub-shrub to 70 cm with a pungent smell when crushed, and pale mauve flowers mostly from spring to autumn. It grows on rocky and forest margins with some direct light.

name: Coprosma quadrifida
description: A slender, widely branching shrub whose stems are often spiny. It grows beside creeks in damp woodland and forest.
care_note: The stems are often spiny.

name: Coronidium elatum
description: An erect subshrub with woolly branches and large white everlasting daisy flower heads in spring and summer. It grows in eucalypt forest, often in mountain country.

name: Coronidium scorpioides
description: An ascending perennial herb with a basal rosette and papery daisy flowers in spring. It grows in well-drained open forest.

name: Correa lawrenceana
description: A small to medium shrub to about 3 m that flowers from autumn to late spring and attracts honeyeating birds. It is reasonably hardy in moist, well-drained soil.
care_note: It does well in a protected position and needs moist, well-drained soil.

name: Corymbia calophylla
description: A large tree of south-west Western Australia with a rounded crown and cream flowers in mid-summer. Its large nuts feed parrots and cockatoos.

name: Corymbia gummifera
description: A tree to 30 m of dry forest and woodland on poor sandy and sandstone soils along the east coast.

name: Corymbia maculata
description: A tall eucalypt with smooth, spotted cream to blue-grey bark and white flowers that honeyeaters visit. It is for large properties.
care_note: It can grow very large, up to 50 m in the wild, and koalas eat its leaves.

name: Corymbia tessellaris
description: A large tree with a solitary trunk, widely branching crown and hanging foliage, found in open woodland on plains and gentle country. It flowers from November to January.

name: Craspedia variabilis
description: An erect herb with narrow leaves at the base and golden-yellow ball-shaped flower heads on stalks up to 50 cm, from early spring to early summer. It grows in woodland, forest and grassland.

name: Cryptocarya triplinervis
description: A small to medium rainforest tree, mostly of warmer coastal rainforest, with yellowish flowers and purple-black fruit.

name: Cyathea australis
description: A hardy tree fern with a trunk to about 10 m and finely divided fronds up to 4.5 m, with a rough frond stalk. It grows in semi-shade and in full sun if the roots stay moist.
care_note: Unlike the soft tree fern, sawn trunk sections will not regrow roots.

name: Cyperus polystachyos
description: A tufted sedge with triangular stems 10 to 60 cm tall and brownish spikelets, found in open, often disturbed places. It is native and is easily confused with other flat-sedges.

name: Dampiera stricta
description: A suckering, soft-wooded perennial with sky-blue to mauve flowers, suited to rockeries, containers and cottage gardens. It looks best in clumps.
pruning: Remove spent flowers to encourage more blooms.

name: Daviesia latifolia
description: A multi-stemmed medium to large shrub with leathery leaf-like stems and clusters of yellow pea flowers marked reddish-brown, followed by flattened pods.

name: Daviesia leptophylla
description: An open, upright, broom-like shrub with narrow leaves and yellow flowers marked with maroon, followed by small triangular pods. It suits planting under eucalypts and needs good drainage.

name: Daviesia ulicifolia
description: A rigid, very prickly shrub with sharp phyllodes and yellow-orange pea flowers. Its dense prickles give small birds shelter.
care_note: Keep it away from paths because it is very prickly.

name: Dendrophthoe vitellina
description: A native mistletoe that hangs from many hosts, often Myrtaceae, in forest and woodland.

name: Dianella brevicaulis
description: A tufted perennial to 50 cm that grows in coastal, near-coastal and lakeside habitats in the south.

name: Dianella longifolia
description: A tufted perennial with leaves to 80 cm long, widespread in forest across most of Australia. Its height varies by variety, from 0.5 to 1.5 m.

name: Dillwynia cinerascens
description: A low to erect shrub with small pea flowers in short clusters, found in dry forest and woodland on loam to clay soils.

name: Diplarrena moraea
description: A clumping, rhizomatous herb with long flat leaves and flower stems 20 to 100 cm tall. It grows naturally in heath and forest in the south-east.

name: Disphyma crassifolium
description: A low, spreading succulent groundcover with pink daisy flowers in spring and summer. It copes with salt, sand and drought.

name: Dodonaea triquetra
description: A narrow shrub with papery fruit capsules that ripen purple-red on female plants. It is very hardy and often used in bush regeneration.
pruning: It can be pruned for density.

name: Drosera binata
description: A carnivorous plant with branching sticky leaves that uncoil like ferns, flowering in spring and summer. It grows in a pot kept moist in a saucer of water, or in a bog garden.

name: Drynaria rigidula
description: A rainforest fern that creeps or forms clumps, with a scaly rhizome, short lobed sterile fronds that catch litter and long fertile fronds. It is listed as Endangered in NSW.
care_note: It is listed as Endangered under the NSW Biodiversity Conservation Act.

name: Drypetes deplanchei
description: A small to medium tree with stiff toothed leaves and fleshy orange to red fruit ripening in late summer to autumn, found in coastal rainforest.

name: Duboisia myoporoides
description: A shrub or tree up to about 20 m at the edges of rainforest and in regrowth, flowering from winter to spring.

toxic.note: It is reported to be toxic to stock and humans if eaten.

name: Duma florulenta
description: An intricate, rounded shrub with grey-green striate stems that often end in a spine, growing 1 to 3 m high and wide. It grows in seasonally flooded low-lying areas with grey clay soils.

name: Elaeocarpus grandis
description: A large rainforest tree of lowland and riverside forest on the east coast, known for its blue fruit. It needs room to grow.

name: Elaeocarpus obovatus
description: A rainforest tree with a strongly buttressed trunk, racemes of white flowers whose petals are fringed, and blue fruit. It flowers in spring.

name: Eremophila debilis
description: A very low, almost herbaceous groundcover with white flowers tinged lilac, followed by small purple fruits that look like miniature apples. It does well in a shady spot and forms a dense carpet.
pruning: Pinch out the growing tips for the densest growth.
care_note: It benefits from a shady spot with extra moisture. Plant at 1.5 m centres for a dense carpet. It is listed as critically endangered in Victoria.

name: Eremophila latrobei
description: A small to medium shrub with tubular red to purplish flowers from winter to early summer. It prefers full sun and well-drained soil.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil.

name: Eremophila longifolia
description: A hardy, rounded small tree or large shrub with fissured bark and tubular flowers in pink through to brown-red. Honeyeaters and insects visit the nectar, and it suits screening in harsh, inland conditions.
care_note: It suckers, so choose its planting site with care.

name: Eriostemon australasius
description: A small, fairly stiff, upright shrub with greyish-green leaves and waxy pale to mid-pink flowers from late winter to late spring. It likes a semi-shaded spot and soil that is well drained but not dry for long.
care_note: It will not tolerate waterlogging.

name: Eryngium ovinum
description: A clumping perennial with spiky, metallic blue flower heads in summer that dies down in autumn. It suits cottage gardens, borders and rockeries, and the heads can be cut and dried.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil, and is best grown in full sun.

name: Eucalyptus camaldulensis
description: A very large spreading eucalypt with smooth white to multi-coloured bark and blue-grey leaves, found along watercourses. It needs room, and it can drop branches without warning.
care_note: It can drop large branches unexpectedly, so keep it away from buildings and paths.

name: Eucalyptus diversifolia
description: A mallee with smooth bark, glossy leaves and white flowers from late winter to summer, growing on dunes and limestone soils.

name: Eucalyptus fasciculosa
description: A tree with smooth bark that turns from pink to white and masses of cream flowers in summer and autumn. It suits parks and larger gardens for shade.
care_note: In South Australia it needs written SA Water approval before planting in a street, and should be at least 3.5 m from sewer pipes.

name: Eucalyptus globulus
description: A very tall, evergreen eucalypt with cream to yellow flowers in winter and spring. It is grown mainly for timber and as a large habitat tree, so it needs a lot of room.
care_note: It becomes a very tall tree, so choose its site with care. It does not tolerate severe frosts.

name: Eucalyptus incrassata
description: A spreading mallee-type eucalypt with cream to yellow flowers in spring and summer. It is used for screens, windbreaks and erosion control, and responds well to coppicing.
pruning: It responds well to coppicing.
care_note: It needs good drainage. In South Australia it needs written SA Water approval before planting in a street, and should be 3.5 m from sewer pipes.

name: Eucalyptus microcorys
description: A very tall eucalypt with persistent stringy bark and a broad canopy, with white to lemon-yellow flowers in spring and summer. It is a koala food tree and suits parks and large landscapes.
care_note: It is not suited to small gardens and can invade local bushland reserves, so plant it with care.

name: Eucalyptus obliqua
description: A very tall tree with stringy bark, found in cooler, wetter forests on richer soils. White flowers can appear in most months.

name: Eucalyptus pilularis
description: A very tall eucalypt, to 70 m in the wild, that is often dominant in wet sclerophyll and coastal forest. It is too large for most home gardens.

name: Eucalyptus polyanthemos
description: A tree to 20 m that grows in grassy and dry forest woodland on light shallow soils in Victoria and NSW.

name: Eucalyptus regnans
description: The tallest flowering tree in the world, with a smooth white to grey trunk and specimens of 80 m or more. It suits only the largest gardens and parks.
care_note: It is killed outright by severe fire and is too big for all but the largest gardens.

name: Eucalyptus sideroxylon
description: A tree 10 to 30 m tall with hard, deeply furrowed black bark and white, pink or red flowers. It copes with a wide range of soils and climates.

name: Eucalyptus viminalis
description: A tall tree with smooth white limbs and ribbons of shed bark, a main koala food tree. It does best in moist, fertile soil but is fairly hardy once established.
edible: Manna, a sweet crumbly white gum from the bark, is eaten raw in summer.

name: Euroschinus falcatus
description: A small to medium-sized tree of coastal rainforest and its margins.

name: Euryomyrtus ramosissima
description: A small, low to semi-prostrate shrub with tiny leaves and masses of small white to deep rosy-pink flowers. It suits small gardens, rockeries and containers.
pruning: Tip prune after flowering to encourage a bushier plant and more flowers the next season.

name: Eutaxia microphylla
description: A variable shrub, often low, dense and intricate, whose smaller stems are often spiny. It grows in mallee and woodland.
care_note: Its smaller stems are often spiny.

name: Exocarpos cupressiformis
description: A shrub or small tree with weeping, conifer-like foliage that is a root parasite, often found near eucalypts. The swollen red stalk under its small nut is edible.
edible: The enlarged, usually bright red flower stalk is eaten; the small nut attached to it is the true fruit.
care_note: Plants are hard to propagate and generally do not survive being planted out.

name: Ficus macrophylla
description: A very large spreading strangler fig with a buttressed trunk and glossy leaves. It is too large for ordinary suburban gardens but is good in parks and large containers.
care_note: Its vigorous roots can damage pavements and house foundations, so do not plant it in a suburban garden.

name: Ficus rubiginosa
description: A small to large spreading tree, often buttressed, growing on rocky sites in open forest. It needs a lot of space.

name: Gahnia sieberiana
description: A large tussock-forming sedge with long arching leaves whose rough edges can cut. It forms clumps up to about 2 m across and suits damp sites, as a substitute for pampas grass.
care_note: The leaf edges are rough and can give a painful cut if handled carelessly.

name: Gaudium laevigatum
description: A large bushy shrub to about 5 m with grey-green leaves and white flowers from late winter to spring. It copes with salt spray and hard pruning.
pruning: It tolerates severe pruning.
care_note: It is weedy outside its natural range. It is declared in SA and an environmental weed in southern WA, so please avoid planting it there.

name: Gaudium myrsinoides
description: A dense, fast-growing medium shrub with white or pink flowers in spring. It copes with poorly drained sites and makes a screen or hedge.
pruning: It responds well to pruning.
care_note: Its vigorous roots can crowd out nearby plants.

name: Geitonoplesium cymosum
description: A twining or sprawling vine with stems to about 8 m, found in rainforest and forest.

name: Glochidion ferdinandi
description: A fast-growing, dense shade tree with cheese-shaped fruit that opens to red seeds eaten by birds. It is a larval host for butterflies and is almost maintenance free.
care_note: It may sucker if its roots are disturbed.

name: Glycine clandestina
description: A slender twining climber with mauve to pale pink or white pea flowers in winter and spring. It is not vigorous and is rarely sold.

name: Grevillea alpina
description: A variable evergreen shrub, from low and spreading to tall and upright, with clusters of cream, yellow, orange or red flowers for much of the year. It copes with frost and dry spells once established.
care_note: Forms vary a lot in size, and it is not suited to humid subtropical or tropical areas.

name: Grevillea buxifolia
description: A small to medium rounded shrub with small glossy leaves and clusters of grey, hairy spider-type flowers in late winter and spring. It does well in well-drained soil.
care_note: Avoid misting, because its hairy stems and leaves can get fungal problems.

name: Grevillea linearifolia
description: An upright, spreading shrub with white spider-type flower clusters through most of the year. It does well in free-draining soil.
pruning: Pruning encourages a tidier shape and more flowering.
care_note: It flowers most of the year if it is not allowed to dry out.

name: Grevillea speciosa
description: A small to medium shrub with bright red spider flowers mostly in spring, found only around Sydney. Sandy soil suits it best.
pruning: Light pruning keeps plants dense and flowering well.

name: Grevillea wickhamii
description: A variable grevillea from northern and western Australia, from low shrubs to spindly trees. The commonly grown subspecies is about 2.5 m high and wide and flowers from winter to spring.

name: Hakea decurrens
description: A spreading shrub to small tree with rigid needle-like leaves and white, sometimes pink-tinged flowers in winter and spring. It grows on sandy or rocky sites in dry forest and heath.

name: Hakea rostrata
description: A spreading or rounded shrub with needle-like leaves and small white flowers from winter to spring, followed by woody beaked fruit. It grows in heathland on sandy soils.

name: Hakea sericea
description: A tall, prickly shrub with fragrant white flowers in winter and spring. It makes a dense barrier but is a serious weed in South Africa.
care_note: Keep it away from paths, because its foliage is prickly.

name: Hakea teretifolia
description: A rigid shrub with needle-like leaves and cream-white to yellow flowers, easy to grow in a sunny spot. Planted in clumps it shelters small birds.
pruning: It can be pruned for a tighter shape.
care_note: Its leaves are sharp.

name: Heptapleurum actinophyllum
description: A multi-trunked tree with large glossy leaflets that radiate from one point and deep red flower spikes at the top of the foliage. Birds spread its seeds, and it is regarded as an environmental weed outside its home range.
pruning: If it grows too tall, heavy pruning to near ground level brings vigorous new growth.
care_note: Brisbane City Council lists it as a Council Pest Vegetation and it is regarded as an environmental weed in south-eastern Queensland and New South Wales; its roots can damage pipes and footpaths, so plant it well away from them.

name: Hibbertia dentata
description: A light climbing or trailing plant to about 2 m with dark toothed leaves and bright yellow flowers from late winter to late spring. It copes with shade and can be used as a groundcover.
care_note: It needs reasonable drainage but should not be left to dry out.

name: Hibbertia sericea
description: A small, upright evergreen shrub with yellow open flowers in spring. It attracts butterflies and native insects and responds to pruning.
pruning: It responds to pruning.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil.

name: Hibbertia vestita
description: A prostrate shrub with hairy leaves and bright yellow flowers about 20 mm across. It is a good low plant for a well-drained sunny spot.
care_note: It needs good drainage and appreciates extra water in dry spells.

name: Hibiscus tiliaceus
description: A fast-growing, dense evergreen coastal tree with large leaves and yellow summer flowers. It handles salt spray, poor drainage and bore water.
edible: Young shoots are eaten as a vegetable.

name: Homalanthus populifolius
description: A small tree or shrub with heart-shaped leaves that age to red or purple and a rounded canopy. It is a quick pioneer of disturbed ground and can become weedy.
care_note: It exudes a milky sap, so take care when pruning, and it can become a weed in disturbed areas.

name: Hovea acutifolia
description: A small to medium upright shrub with rusty-hairy new growth and blue to purple pea flowers in spring.

name: Hoya australis
description: A moderately vigorous climber with thick glossy leaves and fragrant white flowers with red centres in late spring and summer. It suits pots and baskets.
care_note: Good drainage is essential, and in cool areas it needs frost protection.

name: Jacksonia scoparia
description: A tall shrub or small tree with an open, weeping habit, grey-green winged stems with scale leaves, and scented yellow pea flowers in late spring and summer.
pruning: A light prune after flowering encourages dense growth and more flowers.
care_note: It needs reliable drainage and space to spread; it is a weed in parts of Victoria.

name: Jagera pseudorhus
description: A small rainforest tree with a rounded canopy, whose fruit is eaten by many birds. The hairs on its seed capsules irritate skin.
care_note: Avoid touching the fruit capsules, because their stiff hairs irritate.

name: Kennedia rubicunda
description: A vigorous climber or mat-former with glossy leaves and clusters of deep red pea flowers, mostly in spring and summer. It can cover several metres.
pruning: Periodic pruning keeps it in check and trained.
care_note: It is reported as a weed in Tasmania.

name: Kunzea capitata
description: A small spreading or erect woody shrub, usually 0.5 to 1 m tall, that flowers in spring. It is hardy in well-drained, moist soils and takes frost.

name: Kunzea pomifera
description: A creeping, prostrate evergreen shrub that forms a dense mat, with white flowers in spring and edible berries in late summer. It suits coastal gardens, embankments and sand stabilisation.
pruning: It responds well to pruning.
edible: The berries are eaten as a bush food, with a flavour likened to spicy apples.
care_note: It is recommended for exposed coastal sites and self-layers as it spreads.

name: Lagunaria patersonia
description: A medium to large tree, 12 to 20 m, with grey-green leaves and pink to mauve flowers in spring and early summer. The seed capsules hold fibres that irritate skin.

toxic.note: The fibres in the seed capsules can irritate the skin, so wear gloves when handling them.

care_note: It is native to Lord Howe and Norfolk Islands only, and has naturalised in parts of mainland NSW.

name: Lepidosperma gladiatum
description: A clump-forming sedge with stems 45 to 100 cm tall that grows on coastal dunes and headlands in sandy soil.

name: Leptospermum continentale
description: A shrub with small prickly-tipped leaves and white flowers in spring and early summer, found in sandy or swampy soils of forests and open sites.

name: Leptospermum lanigerum
description: A shrub or small tree with small hairy leaves and white flowers about 15 mm across from October to January. It grows in open woodland, sandy swamps and along watercourses.

name: Leptospermum scoparium
description: A hardy medium shrub with small white flowers in spring, popular with bees and beekeepers. It suits sandy, free-draining soil.
care_note: It is prone to webbing caterpillar and scale insects.

name: Leschenaultia biloba
description: A short-lived, mound-forming groundcover with blue flowers, from Western Australia. It needs sharp drainage and is hard to keep going in humid eastern Australia.
care_note: It has proven difficult to keep going in cultivation, especially in humid eastern Australia.

name: Leucochrysum albicans
description: A tufted plant with narrow grey-green leaves and papery daisy flowers held singly on slender stems, mostly in spring and summer. It suits sunny, well-drained spots in temperate gardens.

name: Leucopogon parviflorus
description: A bushy shrub or small tree with small white winter and spring flowers followed by white edible berries. It is seldom grown because it is hard to propagate and keep.

name: Linospadix monostachyus
description: A slender, slow-growing rainforest palm with a thin trunk, green flower spikes and small red berries. It suits shady gardens and pots.
edible: Red berries are eaten, and new shoots are eaten raw or cooked, according to a local plant guide.
care_note: It likes moist, well-composted soil, and cutting the growing bud kills the palm.

name: Linum marginale
description: A short-lived, clumping perennial with slender stems and sky-blue star-shaped flowers. It dies back in late summer and regrows from the base, and suits borders and mixed native plantings.
pruning: Cut it to the ground in autumn.
edible: The seeds in the seed pods are edible.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil, and can be mistaken for native bluebells (Wahlenbergia).

name: Lithotoma axillaris
description: An erect or ascending perennial herb to 50 cm with bright blue to mauve flowers that grows in cracks of rocky cliffs and is increasingly popular in gardens.
care_note: Its foliage and sap are a severe irritant to skin and eyes, so handle with care.

name: Lobelia purpurascens
description: A creeping herb that spreads by white rhizomes in shady, wet places and shaded lawns.
care_note: It contains the alkaloid lobeline.

name: Lomandra multiflora
description: A clumping, grass-like plant with narrow dark green leaves and small cream flower heads on separate male and female plants. It is hardy and suits dry gardens and embankments.
pruning: It responds well to hard pruning.

name: Lomatia myricoides
description: A shrub or small tree 2 to 5 m tall that often grows along watercourses or in forest on the coast and ranges.

name: Lomatia silaifolia
description: A shrub with finely divided leaves and summer flowers, widespread in heath, forest and woodland on the coast and tablelands.

name: Lophostemon suaveolens
description: A large tree with red-brown fibrous bark and leaves in whorls, found in swampy forest and on alluvial flats. White flowers appear in spring and early summer.

name: Lysiana exocarpi
description: A spreading to pendent parasitic shrub with narrow leaves and mostly red flowers in summer, living on a wide range of host trees. It cannot be grown without a host.

name: Melaleuca armillaris
description: A shrub or small tree to 5 m that grows in coastal heath, often on headlands, and flowers in summer.

name: Melaleuca ericifolia
description: A tall shrub or small tree with papery bark, fine dark leaves and white spikes that are bountiful in spring. It can form dense thickets in wetlands and suits hedgerows and windbreaks.
pruning: Prune behind the spent flowers to keep plants from becoming straggly.

name: Melaleuca lanceolata
description: A medium evergreen tree with a dense, spreading canopy, a rough trunk and white bottlebrush flowers in spring and summer. It tolerates coastal exposure and dry conditions, so it suits shade, windbreaks and screens.
care_note: Plant it at least 3.5 m from sewer mains, connections and pipes.

name: Melaleuca nodosa
description: A shrub 1 to 4 m high with corky to papery bark, rigid leaves and white to yellow flowers in spring and summer. It grows in coastal heath and dry sclerophyll forest.

name: Melaleuca squamea
description: A shrub to 3 m with scaly bark and mauve to purple flower heads in spring. It is useful as a screen or gap filler and handles frost, drought and poor drainage.
pruning: A light annual trim promotes bushy growth.
care_note: It does not do well in lime-based or saline soils.

name: Melaleuca styphelioides
description: A shrub or tree to 20 m that grows beside streams on the coast of NSW and Queensland and flowers in summer.

name: Melia azedarach
description: A fast-growing deciduous shade tree with lilac-scented pink flowers and clusters of yellow berries. It spreads freely by seed and can become a weed.

toxic.note: The yellow fruit is poisonous if eaten; some reports say a few fruits can be fatal to people, and ripe berries have poisoned dogs and livestock.

care_note: It is a prolific seeder that can become weedy, so avoid planting it near bushland and pull seedlings early.

name: Melicytus dentatus
description: A prickly, spreading shrub or small tree with scented pale yellow flowers in late winter and spring and berries that birds and lizards eat. It can be clipped as a hedge.
pruning: Prune periodically to keep it dense; it can be grown as a hedge.
edible: The berries are reported to be edible.

name: Microlaena stipoides
description: A slender, soft, evergreen tufting grass with a weeping habit and green flower panicles in spring and summer. It can replace exotic grasses in mixed plantings and is a food plant for native butterfly caterpillars.

name: Microsorum pustulatum
description: A scrambling fern with a creeping rhizome and leathery, light green fronds that are simple or lobed, growing on rocks or tree trunks near rainforest.

name: Muellerina eucalyptoides
description: A spreading to hanging shrub that grows as a parasite, usually on eucalypts. It flowers mainly in summer.
care_note: It is a parasite and lives on the branches of its host tree, usually a eucalypt.

name: Myoporum boninense
description: A shrub to 2 m, prostrate to erect, of coastal heath, cliffs and dunes.

name: Myrsine howittiana
description: A shrub or small tree with smooth grey bark, found in rainforest and the margins of moist forest on the coast and lower ranges.

name: Myrsine variabilis
description: A shrub or small tree with shiny green leaves that can be toothed and almost prickly when young. It grows naturally from beside mangrove swamps up to about 1000 m altitude.

name: Nothofagus cunninghamii
description: A rainforest tree with small, dark green, rhomboid leaves and bronze new growth. It is slow to grow in gardens, and prunes well, so it is used for bonsai.
pruning: It prunes well; tip prune in late summer to keep size and shape and encourage spring growth.
care_note: It needs regular deep watering and heavy mulch, and does not tolerate poor soils that dry out easily.

name: Olearia axillaris
description: A dense, compact evergreen shrub with cream daisy flowers in autumn. It is very hardy in coastal gardens and makes a good hedge or windbreak.
pruning: It responds well to pruning and can be clipped as a hedge or screen.

name: Olearia lirata
description: A shrub with greyish-white branchlets and daisy flowers from late winter to summer. It grows in moist forest and subalpine areas.

name: Ozothamnus obcordatus
description: An erect shrub of heath on stony ridges and shallow gravelly soils, flowering from spring into early summer.

name: Pandanus tectorius
description: A branching, tough coastal tree with stilt roots, long spiny-edged leaves and large pineapple-like fruit on female plants. It is highly salt and wind resistant.
edible: Ripe fruit segments and seeds can be roasted and eaten.
care_note: It grows large and has spiny leaves, so keep it away from buildings, paths and drains.

name: Parsonsia straminea
description: A woody vine that climbs by twining stems and aerial roots, with flowers for most of the year and long capsules.

name: Patersonia fragilis
description: A tufted native iris with narrow twisted leaves and violet-blue flowers that open in the morning and close by early afternoon. It suits rockeries, water features and bog gardens.
care_note: It is reported to tolerate dry conditions for less than a week.

name: Pelargonium rodneyanum
description: A small tuberous perennial herb with deep rosy-magenta flowers in summer and autumn. It is tough once established and does well in reasonably well-drained soils.

name: Persoonia juniperina
description: An erect to spreading shrub to about 2 m with narrow, stiff, sharp-tipped leaves and yellow flowers in summer, found in heath and forest on silica-rich soils.
care_note: Its leaves are sharp-tipped.

name: Persoonia linearis
description: A large shrub or small tree with fine, papery blackish bark, narrow soft leaves and small yellow flowers, followed by green fruit in grape-like clusters.

name: Persoonia pinifolia
description: A large shrub with long pine-like leaves, small yellow flowers in the leaf axils and green fruit in grape-like clusters. It is difficult to propagate.

name: Petalostigma pubescens
description: A shrub or small tree to 10 m with grey underleaves and orange-yellow fruit that grows in dry rainforest or open forest.

name: Phebalium squamulosum
description: A small to medium shrub with bright green to grey-green foliage that flowers in early spring. It does best in a well-drained, slightly sheltered spot.

name: Phebalium woombye
description: A small to medium shrub, up to about 2 m high and 1.5 m wide, with some completely prostrate forms. It flowers from late winter into spring.

name: Pimelea humilis
description: A low erect or straggling shrub to 50 cm with small hairless leaves and whitish flowers in heads. It grows in dry open forest and heath.

name: Pimelea linifolia
description: A variable small shrub with narrow blue-green leaves and heads of white, sometimes pink, flowers in spring. It is pretty but can be hard to keep in gardens.
pruning: Prune after flowering to keep it compact.
care_note: It is toxic to animals if eaten, and needs well-drained soil in gardens.

name: Piper hederaceum
description: A native climber of eastern New South Wales and Queensland, recorded from the north coast down to the south coast of New South Wales.

name: Pittosporum angustifolium
description: A shrub or tree with drooping branches, fragrant yellow to cream flowers in winter and spring, and stiff narrow leaves. It grows on sandy soils in woodland and mallee.

name: Pittosporum bicolor
description: An upright, fairly dense shrub or tree with grey-backed leaves and yellow bell flowers marked with maroon. It grows naturally in mountain forests and fern gullies.

name: Pittosporum revolutum
description: An erect, fast-growing shrub with fragrant cream-yellow flowers, used as a hedge or screen.
pruning: Prune after fruiting to encourage a rounded shape.
care_note: It is reported to be weedy in some areas, so plant with caution.

name: Pittosporum undulatum
description: A dense evergreen tree with fragrant white flowers in spring and orange berries that birds eat and spread. Outside its natural range it is a serious bushland weed.
care_note: It is a declared weed in NSW and WA and invades bushland elsewhere, so please do not plant it near bushland.

name: Platycerium bifurcatum
description: An epiphytic fern with flat shield-like nest leaves and forked, antler-like fronds. It is mounted on a board or tree trunk, or grown in a basket, in a shady spot.
care_note: Keep it from drying out, give it filtered sun and shelter from frost.

name: Platycerium superbum
description: A large epiphytic fern with broad, upright nest fronds that hug the host and long, hanging, forked fertile fronds. It grows well mounted on a tree or board in filtered light.
care_note: Soak it about once a week, adjusting for rain, and avoid keeping the centre wet because that can cause rot.

name: Platysace lanceolata
description: An upright or spreading shrub with lance-shaped leaves and white to cream flower umbels from autumn to spring that draw bees and butterflies.

name: Podocarpus elatus
description: A medium to large rainforest tree with a blue-black fleshy fruit stalk, grown for its timber and as an ornamental.

name: Polyscias elegans
description: A tall, sparingly branched rainforest tree with large compound leaves that smell of celery when crushed. It regrows quickly after disturbance and its fruit feeds birds.

name: Polystichum proliferum
description: A tufted fern with dark green, finely divided fronds 50 to 80 cm long that form small plantlets on the frond axis. In the wild it forms large colonies in cool mountain forest.

name: Pomaderris aspera
description: A tall shrub with loose panicles of greenish-yellow flowers, found along streams and in moist gullies in the ranges.

name: Prostanthera lasianthos
description: An erect shrub or medium tree with white flowers from November to February, growing along watercourses and moist gullies in wet forest. It also colonises disturbed sites such as roadsides.

name: Pseuderanthemum variabile
description: A low, creeping perennial with mauve to white flowers that suits shady spots and pots. It self-sows freely and is a caterpillar food plant for several butterflies.
pruning: It can be cut back to ground level if needed.

name: Psilotum nudum
description: A leafless-looking fern with yellow-green, ridged, branching stems 15 to 60 cm long that grows in tufts in rock crevices in forest.

name: Psychotria loniceroides
description: A shrub or small tree with hairy young growth, small white flowers in summer and whitish ribbed fruit, found in warm rainforest and wet forest.

name: Pteridium esculentum
description: A tall, coarse fern with stiff erect fronds that spreads by long creeping rhizomes. On cleared land it can form large colonies that are hard to get rid of.
care_note: On cleared land it spreads by rhizomes into large colonies that are hard to eradicate.

name: Pultenaea daphnoides
description: An upright shrub with deep yellow, red-marked pea flowers in late winter and spring. It likes good drainage.
pruning: Prune lightly after flowering.

name: Pultenaea gunnii
description: A pea-flowered native shrub of south-eastern Australia, recorded in NSW, Victoria and Tasmania.

name: Pultenaea pedunculata
description: A prostrate, mat-forming shrub with softly hairy stems and small yellow pea flowers, which root where they touch the ground. It suits rockeries and shallow soil.
pruning: Prune after flowering to keep a dense bush with more flowers the following season.
care_note: It prefers moist but well-drained soil and should not be grown in dense shade. It is listed as threatened (Vulnerable) in NSW.

name: Pultenaea scabra
description: A small to medium shrub with densely hairy stems and clusters of pea flowers in spring. It suits a sunny or semi-shaded spot with moist, well-drained soil.

name: Rhagodia candolleana
description: A spreading or upright coastal shrub to 4 m with small elliptic to arrow-shaped leaves and fleshy fruits. It grows naturally on saline or sandy ground near the coast.

name: Rhodamnia rubescens
description: A rainforest tree, often a medium to large shrub, with white flowers in late winter and spring and shiny black berries that birds eat. Myrtle rust has made it critically endangered in the wild.
care_note: Myrtle rust kills it and it may host the disease in gardens, so please check planted specimens regularly.

name: Richea pandanifolia
description: A tall palm-like Tasmanian plant on a single stem with long tapering leaves crowded at the top and white or deep pink flowers. It is grown for its foliage, and suits a container in cool climates.
care_note: It prefers well-composted, moist soil with reasonable drainage and a sheltered position.

name: Ricinocarpos pinifolius
description: A small mounded shrub with soft pine-like leaves and starry white flowers in spring, which are also used as cut flowers. It does best in sandy, well-drained soil.
pruning: A light tip prune after flowering helps maintain its shape.

name: Rubus moluccanus
description: A tall, prickly scrambling shrub that forms thickets, with white or pink flowers in spring and summer and bright red fruit. It suits larger properties because it spreads.
pruning: It responds well to pruning, so regular pruning keeps it to a manageable size.
edible: The red fruit is edible, but fine hairs on it can irritate the mouth or skin.
care_note: Its stiff prickles and spreading thickets make it unsuitable for small gardens.

name: Rubus parvifolius
description: A scrambling shrub with stems about a metre long, leaves in threes with white woolly undersides, and pink to red flowers followed by small round red fruit.

name: Sabdariffa heterophylla
description: A medium to large open shrub with large white, pink or yellow hibiscus flowers with a deep red centre. Each flower lasts a day or two but new ones open over a long season.
edible: The flower buds can be made into jam, and other parts have been eaten.
care_note: The hairy seed capsules can irritate skin, so please handle them with care.

name: Sambucus gaudichaudiana
description: An evergreen shrub up to 2 m with divided leaves, sprays of small white flowers in summer and white fruit. It grows in moister sclerophyll forest.

name: Smilax australis
description: A prickly climber with stems up to 8 m that forms dense thickets in forest and heath.
care_note: Its stems are usually prickly.

name: Solanum laciniatum
description: An erect, prickle-free shrub with purplish branches, found on stabilised sand dunes, creeks and road verges, flowering from spring to summer.

name: Solanum prinophyllum
description: A sprawling, prickly herb to 50 cm with deeply lobed leaves, lilac-blue flowers and green or purple berries, found in forest and its margins. Take care around its prickles.
care_note: Its stems and leaves are prickly.

name: Stypandra glauca
description: A clumping, evergreen perennial with stiff strap leaves and nodding blue flowers with yellow centres in late winter and spring. It suits borders, rockeries and bushy native plantings.
pruning: Prune after flowering to keep the clump dense.

name: Syncarpia glomulifera
description: A tall tree with thick fibrous bark and leaves white-hairy underneath, often found near rainforest edges and in wet forest. Its durable timber has long been used for wharves.

name: Synoum glandulosum
description: A large shrub to small tree with glossy compound leaves, small scented white flowers and red-brown capsules with red seeds that attract birds.
care_note: It needs reliable moisture during dry times.

name: Telopea truncata
description: An upright shrub, about 3 m tall, sometimes a small tree, with a lignotuber and red flowers from November to February. It suits cooler-climate gardens.
care_note: ANPSA says it needs good drainage but also ample moisture to thrive.

name: Tetratheca ciliata
description: A slender upright shrub to about a metre with small leaves in whorls and fragrant deep lilac-pink flowers in spring. It grows in heath and open forest.

name: Thysanotus tuberosus
description: A tuberous perennial with narrow leaves and branched stems of mauve to purple fringed flowers, each lasting one day. New flowers keep opening over spring and early summer.

name: Todea barbara
description: A tree-like fern with a broad dark trunk to 3 m and leathery fronds 0.5 to 2.5 m long, growing in damp mountain rainforest and along streams.

name: Trema tomentosum
description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with rough light green leaves, and shiny black berries from late summer to autumn. It grows on rainforest margins and regrowth.
care_note: Recorded as toxic to stock, though animals usually eat it only in dry conditions.

name: Trichodesma zeylanicum
description: An upright annual or perennial herb about 1 m high with blue flowers, which are occasionally white, from May to October. It grows in open sandy or rocky country.

name: Tripladenia cunninghamii
description: A native herb to 40 cm that grows in rainforest and wet forest on the north coast of NSW and in Queensland.

name: Trochocarpa laurina
description: A compact shrub or crooked tree with glossy dark leaves, slender spikes of white flowers and purple-black fruit, found in gullies and wet forest.

name: Veronica gracilis
description: A slender rhizomatous perennial herb with small pale lilac or blue flowers with darker veins. It grows in grassland and grassy woodland, often in swampy or damp sites.

name: Viminaria juncea
description: A small multi-trunked tree with a pendulous look and yellow pea flowers in spring and summer. It resembles European broom, and suits planting around small pools and ponds.
care_note: It flowers best with extra water and can die back in dry periods.

name: Westringia eremicola
description: A shrub to 1.5 m that grows in sandy mallee soils and flowers through the year.

name: Xanthorrhoea australis
description: A very slow-growing grass tree with a thick, often branched trunk, a skirt of wiry leaves and a tall cream flower spike. It is a feature plant for well-drained soil.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil and is prone to Phytophthora dieback.

name: Xanthorrhoea minor
description: A small grass tree with no trunk above ground, forming clumps of arching, firm leaves with cream flower spikes in spring. It grows slowly and suits containers.
care_note: It is slow to flower from seed and needs reliable drainage; plants are reported to be susceptible to Phytophthora.

name: Xerochrysum viscosum
description: A clumping evergreen daisy with sticky foliage and yellow to gold flowers through spring and summer. It suits sunny, well-drained beds and attracts insects.
pruning: Prune back after flowering to encourage new flowering shoots and keep the plant bushy.
